text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The U.S. Ambassador to Kenya Prudence Bushnell says her country is extremely disappointed with the way bilateral aid has been used so far and indicates a shift in American policy to the use of non-governmental organisations and private investment.
- The Kenya Finance Bank goes into liquidation after protracted efforts by the statutory manager Joshua Kabacho to revive it, prove fruitless.

- In a bid to promote secondary market trading of Treasury Bills, the Central Bank of Kenya raises the minimum amount of money for investment in government paper to one million shillings from 50,000 shillings, in both primary and open market operations.

- Kenya's ruling party Kenya African National Union (KANU), says the much talked about existence of A and B members within the party is the creation of opposition politicians who are anxious to see the ruling party disintegrate.
- About 80,000 people from four districts in Rift Valley Province face starvation if the government does not provide famine relief to the areas between now and December.
- Five primary schools in Tharaka Nithi district (Eastern Province) close down following boundary clashes between two neighbouring communities of Igembe and Tharaka.
- A Nairobi business tycoon Amin Alibhai is wanted by the British police for escaping from a British jail where he was serving a jail term.
